title: Build the four-subcommand command tree
description:
**Blueprint:** `specs/features/spec-index/spec-index-blueprint.md` — delta **CLI**, section "Command Surface in container-spec-cli (added — command tree)".
**FRD:** `specs/features/spec-index/spec-index-frd.md`.
**Delivery:** staged (stage 2 of 3); this feature's closure set is `bd list --label feature-spec-validation-cli`.

Present the engine as the four-subcommand surface REQ-SPEC-011 fixes,
converting between the module's finding and index models and the process's
stdout and exit status.

This component holds **no domain logic** — a check that lived here would be
unavailable to a future API or MCP wrapper. That is binding Change Guidance
in `specs/architecture/container-spec-cli.md`, not a style preference.

## Retro

Before closing this item, record retro findings on this issue —
one `bd comment` per finding, prefixed `retro:` — following the
findings capture protocol in `rfcs/findings-capture.md`. Friction
only: what happened plus the item or spec text that caused it (or
the gap where guidance was missing). No analysis, no RFCs — the
plan's final DoD item runs the aggregated retro.
design:
- Expose the subcommands `index`, `check`, `slug-exists` and `next-id`, and
  list them with their options on `--help` or a bare invocation.
- `check` accepts an optional path and the `--json`, `--strict` and `--only`
  options: `--json` writes the full finding set as JSON to stdout; `--only`
  names a subset of checks by their rule identifiers and runs only those; the
  report distinguishes a passed check from an un-requested one.
- WHEN a check run produces at least one `error`, exit non-zero. WHEN it
  produces only `warning` or `unverified` findings, exit zero unless
  `--strict` is set.
- `index` exits zero after building an index that contains parse failures,
  and accepts the output-path option from the CACHE item.
- `slug-exists` reports whether a corpus member declares the given slug and,
  if so, its path. `next-id` returns the next identifier for a numbered type,
  via #Numbering.
- WHEN a command or flag is added, its `--help` text derives from the same
  declaration that defines it, so the two cannot drift (container Change
  Guidance).

Anchors: `cli/cmd`; [[adr-015]] names `cobra` for the command tree. Renders
#Findings and reads the `SpecIndex`. Snapshot cases live under
`cli/testdata/cases/`; `specs/architecture/container-spec-cli.md` requires
that when observable output changes, the snapshot regeneration script is run
and every resulting diff reviewed before commit.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] `index`, `check`, `slug-exists` and `next-id` exist and are listed with
      their options on `--help` and on a bare invocation (**proves
      AC-SPEC-011.2 and AC-SPEC-011.5**, integration).
- [ ] `index` accepts the output-path option and exits zero on an index
      containing parse failures (**proves AC-SPEC-011.1 and AC-SPEC-002.5**,
      integration).
- [ ] `slug-exists` reports presence and path (**proves AC-SPEC-011.3**,
      integration); `next-id` returns the next identifier (**proves
      AC-SPEC-011.4**, integration).
- [ ] `--json` writes the full finding set as JSON to stdout (**proves
      AC-SPEC-006.5**, integration).
- [ ] `--only` runs only the named rule identifiers (**proves
      AC-SPEC-006.8**, integration).
- [ ] At least one `error` exits non-zero (**proves AC-SPEC-006.6**,
      integration); only `warning`/`unverified` exits zero unless `--strict`
      (**proves AC-SPEC-006.7**, integration).
- [ ] `--help` text derives from the same declaration that defines each
      command and flag.
- [ ] No domain logic lives in `cli/cmd` — every check is invoked from
      `cli/core` or `cli/profile`.
- [ ] Snapshot cases exist under `cli/testdata/cases/`.
- [ ] Tests cite AC-SPEC-002.5, 006.5–006.8, 011.1–011.5. Tests cite the ACs they verify with an `// AC: AC-SPEC-XXX.Y` comment on the line immediately preceding the test declaration, per `specs/standards/testing-standards.md`.
- [ ] The command tree is recorded in
      `specs/architecture/container-spec-cli.md`, delivered in this same
      change.

metadata.tier_reason: Broad but shallow: ten acceptance criteria over a cobra command tree with the domain logic already built elsewhere. Large est_size, low capability need — each subcommand and exit rule is individually pinned.

title: Persist the index and serve it warm via a content hash
description:
**Blueprint:** `specs/features/spec-index/spec-index-blueprint.md` — delta **CACHE**, section "#Corpus in module-document-core (added — output and cache)".
**FRD:** `specs/features/spec-index/spec-index-frd.md`.
**Delivery:** staged (stage 2 of 3); this feature's closure set is `bd list --label feature-spec-validation-cli`.

Persist the built index to one known file that doubles as the warm cache, so
a CI job publishes the same artifact a later query reads without re-walking
the corpus. This is the container blueprint's "Index cache" data made
concrete.

Staleness is detected by a **content hash** of the index's inputs, not by
modification time. That is a pinned decision (`agent-plugins-igc`), and the
reason is concrete: a fresh CI checkout whose files carry new mtimes but
identical content must still be served warm, which is the condition the
REQ-SPEC-009.1 CI budget depends on.

## Retro

Before closing this item, record retro findings on this issue —
one `bd comment` per finding, prefixed `retro:` — following the
findings capture protocol in `rfcs/findings-capture.md`. Friction
only: what happened plus the item or spec text that caused it (or
the gap where guidance was missing). No analysis, no RFCs — the
plan's final DoD item runs the aggregated retro.
design:
- WHEN asked to build the index, write it to `specs.json` inside the
  configured spec root by default; to a location named by the output-path
  option when given; or to standard output — leaving the default file
  untouched — when the option is `-`.
- WHEN writing to a file, replace any existing file **atomically**, so a
  concurrent reader never observes a partial file.
- Detect staleness by a content hash of the index's inputs, never by mtime.
- WHEN a query or single-document check runs and the persisted index's input
  hash is unchanged since it was written, answer from the persisted index
  without re-walking the corpus.
- IF the persisted index is absent or any corpus input's hash has changed,
  rebuild before answering.
- Produce identical output whether or not a warm index is present, so
  deleting `specs.json` is always safe.

Anchors: `cli/core/corpus` (emission and the content-hash staleness check).

This resolves `specs/architecture/module-document-core.md`'s standing Open
Question on cache invalidation in favour of content hashing; folding that
resolution into the module blueprint belongs to the blueprint-reconciliation
item.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] The index is written to `specs.json` in the configured spec root by
      default (**proves AC-SPEC-010.1**, unit), to the output-path option's
      location when given (**proves AC-SPEC-010.2**, unit), or to stdout
      leaving the default file untouched when the option is `-` (**proves
      AC-SPEC-010.3**, unit).
- [ ] File replacement is atomic — a concurrent reader never sees a partial
      file (**proves AC-SPEC-010.4**, unit).
- [ ] An unchanged input hash is answered from the persisted index with no
      corpus re-walk (**proves AC-SPEC-010.5, AC-SPEC-009.1 and
      AC-SPEC-009.2**, integration).
- [ ] An absent index or any changed input hash triggers a rebuild (**proves
      AC-SPEC-010.6**, integration).
- [ ] A test proves mtime-only change with identical content is still served
      warm (the fresh-CI-checkout condition).
- [ ] Output is identical with and without a warm index present.
- [ ] Tests cite AC-SPEC-009.1, 009.2, 010.1–010.6. Tests cite the ACs they verify with an `// AC: AC-SPEC-XXX.Y` comment on the line immediately preceding the test declaration, per `specs/standards/testing-standards.md`.
- [ ] The index output and warm cache are recorded in
      `specs/architecture/module-document-core.md`, delivered in this same
      change.

metadata.tier_reason: Atomic replacement under concurrent readers plus content-hash staleness detection. Serving a stale index is a silent wrong answer, and the mtime-insensitivity requirement is easy to implement subtly wrong.

title: Load and check specs.toml and select a profile from the registry
description:
**Blueprint:** `specs/features/spec-index/spec-index-blueprint.md` — delta **CFG**, section "Command Surface in container-spec-cli (added — configuration)".
**FRD:** `specs/features/spec-index/spec-index-frd.md`.
**Delivery:** staged (stage 2 of 3); this feature's closure set is `bd list --label feature-spec-validation-cli`.

Resolve and check `specs.toml`, select one profile by name from a **profile
registry**, and report configuration defects through the same finding
machinery as corpus defects.

The profile registry is the customization seam: it maps `[profile].name` to a
`Profile`, holds `spec-driven-dev` as the built-in, and is where a second
taxonomy is wired in — a registry of profiles, each carrying its own single
schema. Configuration is *checked*, not merely loaded: a malformed config is
the first thing an adopter gets wrong.

Realizes `specs/contracts/contract-specs-configuration.md`. That contract's
shape is unchanged by this feature — this is its first implementation.

## Retro

Before closing this item, record retro findings on this issue —
one `bd comment` per finding, prefixed `retro:` — following the
findings capture protocol in `rfcs/findings-capture.md`. Friction
only: what happened plus the item or spec text that caused it (or
the gap where guidance was missing). No analysis, no RFCs — the
plan's final DoD item runs the aggregated retro.
design:
- Hold a registry of available profiles keyed by name, and activate exactly
  the one `[profile].name` selects, passing it the resolved configuration.
- Read configuration from a TOML file at the repository root and resolve
  `[workspace].root` relative to it, determining the spec root, the workspace
  identifier, and — via the activated profile — the union schema and the slug
  patterns its checks apply.
- WHEN `specs.toml` is absent, report the path looked for and exit non-zero,
  inferring no spec root.
- IF the configuration is present but invalid, report each offending key and
  its span, and do **not** fall back to a default for that key. Report every
  defect in one run, validating against the generated
  `cli/core/schema/specs-config.schema.json`.
- IF `[profile].name` names no profile in the registry, report a finding
  listing the registered names.
- Resolve absent `[conventions]` keys from the active profile.

Anchors: new package `cli/cmd`; consumes the generated
`specmodel.SpecsConfig`, the generated config schema, and the profile
registry into which the `spec-driven-dev` profile registers.

`specs/architecture/container-spec-cli.md` Change Guidance: the command
surface must never implement a capability itself — it invokes
`module-document-core` or `module-spec-profile`.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] `[workspace].root` resolves relative to the config file's location
      (**proves AC-SPEC-008.1**, unit).
- [ ] The resolved configuration determines spec root, workspace identifier,
      and — via the activated profile — union schema and slug patterns
      (**proves AC-SPEC-008.2**, unit).
- [ ] An absent `specs.toml` reports the path looked for and exits non-zero
      with no inferred spec root (**proves AC-SPEC-008.3**, integration).
- [ ] An invalid key is reported with its span (**proves AC-SPEC-008.4**,
      unit) and never silently defaulted (**proves AC-SPEC-008.5**, unit).
- [ ] Every configuration defect is reported in one run, not just the first.
- [ ] An unknown `[profile].name` yields a finding listing the registered
      names.
- [ ] Absent `[conventions]` keys resolve from the active profile.
- [ ] Tests cite AC-SPEC-008.1–008.5. Tests cite the ACs they verify with an `// AC: AC-SPEC-XXX.Y` comment on the line immediately preceding the test declaration, per `specs/standards/testing-standards.md`.
- [ ] The Command Surface and the profile registry are recorded in
      `specs/architecture/container-spec-cli.md`, delivered in this same
      change.

metadata.tier_reason: Well-specified against an existing contract and a generated config schema; localized to one new package. Report-every-defect and never-default are clear rules rather than design calls.

title: Discover the corpus and build the SpecIndex
description:
**Blueprint:** `specs/features/spec-index/spec-index-blueprint.md` — delta **CO**, section "#Corpus in module-document-core (added)".
**FRD:** `specs/features/spec-index/spec-index-frd.md`.
**Delivery:** staged (stage 1 of 3); this feature's closure set is `bd list --label feature-spec-validation-cli`.

Walk the spec root, decide membership from frontmatter and declared type,
record exclusions with their reason, detect duplicate slugs, and assemble the
`SpecIndex` every query reads. Corpus orchestrates the parsers but holds no
parsing logic of its own.

This is the largest single item in the feature — it proves fourteen
acceptance criteria — but the blueprint draws no seam inside it, so it is
delivered as one reviewable unit.

**Verification timing:** AC-SPEC-009.3 (a cold 1,000-document build within
the performance budget) is proved here at integration level with CACHE
participating; AC-SPEC-009.7 (cross-platform byte-identical output) is proved
by the BUILD item. Both land later. Determinism is *implemented* here and
cited here where unit-level; the cross-platform proof is BUILD's.

## Retro

Before closing this item, record retro findings on this issue —
one `bd comment` per finding, prefixed `retro:` — following the
findings capture protocol in `rfcs/findings-capture.md`. Friction
only: what happened plus the item or spec text that caused it (or
the gap where guidance was missing). No analysis, no RFCs — the
plan's final DoD item runs the aggregated retro.
design:
- WHEN invoked against a directory, treat every `.md` file beneath it whose
  frontmatter parses and declares a known `type` as a corpus member. Consider
  **only** `.md` files, passing over other files without recording them as
  exclusions.
- IF a `.md` file has no frontmatter or declares an unknown `type`, record it
  as excluded with reason `no-frontmatter` or `unknown-type` respectively,
  reporting the declared type value in the latter case.
- Never read files outside the configured spec root.
- WHEN a single file path is checked, check that file but resolve it against
  the full corpus discovered from the spec root (duplicate-slug detection
  needs the whole corpus).
- Build a `SpecIndex` carrying, per member, its frontmatter and
  repository-relative path, plus `schema_version` and the configured
  `workspace`.
- WHEN a member cannot be parsed, record the failure against it and index
  every other document rather than aborting.
- WHEN two members declare the same slug, compared **without regard to letter
  case**, report a `Finding` against each naming the other's path.
- Emit every path in the index and in findings using forward slashes,
  relative to the repository root, and order entries, exclusions and findings
  deterministically so the same corpus content yields identical output on any
  platform.

Anchors: `cli/core/corpus` (the package the blueprints name for the `Profile`
interface). Consumes #Frontmatter, the Schema Registry, #Findings, and the
generated `specmodel.SpecIndex`. Persisting the index and the warm-cache
staleness check are **not** in this item — they belong to the CACHE item.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] `.md` files whose frontmatter parses and declares a known type are
      members (**proves AC-SPEC-001.1**, unit).
- [ ] A single checked file resolves against the full corpus (**proves
      AC-SPEC-001.2**, integration).
- [ ] Files with no frontmatter are excluded with reason `no-frontmatter`
      (**proves AC-SPEC-001.3**, unit).
- [ ] Files declaring an unknown type are excluded with reason
      `unknown-type` and the declared value reported (**proves
      AC-SPEC-001.4**, unit).
- [ ] No file outside the configured spec root is read (**proves
      AC-SPEC-001.5**, unit).
- [ ] Non-`.md` files are passed over without becoming exclusions (**proves
      AC-SPEC-001.6**, unit).
- [ ] The index carries each member's frontmatter and repository-relative
      path (**proves AC-SPEC-002.1**, unit) and the configured `workspace`
      (**proves AC-SPEC-002.3**, unit).
- [ ] A member that fails to parse is recorded and the rest still indexed
      (**proves AC-SPEC-002.4**, unit).
- [ ] Case-insensitively duplicate slugs yield a `Finding` against each,
      naming the other's path (**proves AC-SPEC-003.3 and AC-SPEC-003.4**,
      unit).
- [ ] A slug query reports whether a member declares it and, if so, its path
      (**proves AC-SPEC-007.2**, integration).
- [ ] A cold 1,000-document build meets the REQ-SPEC-009.3 budget (**proves
      AC-SPEC-009.3**, integration).
- [ ] Paths are emitted forward-slashed and repository-relative (**proves
      AC-SPEC-009.8**, unit); entries, exclusions and findings are ordered
      deterministically.
- [ ] Tests cite all fourteen ACs above. Tests cite the ACs they verify with an `// AC: AC-SPEC-XXX.Y` comment on the line immediately preceding the test declaration, per `specs/standards/testing-standards.md`.
- [ ] The Corpus component is confirmed as built in
      `specs/architecture/module-document-core.md`, delivered in this same
      change.

metadata.tier_reason: The largest item in the feature: fourteen acceptance criteria spanning membership rules, exclusion reasons, case-insensitive duplicate detection, parse-failure tolerance and cross-platform determinism, orchestrating four other components.

title: Derive the next identifier for a numbered type from the index
description:
**Blueprint:** `specs/features/spec-index/spec-index-blueprint.md` — delta **NUM**, section "#Numbering in module-document-core (added)".
**FRD:** `specs/features/spec-index/spec-index-frd.md`.
**Delivery:** staged (stage 1 of 3); this feature's closure set is `bd list --label feature-spec-validation-cli`.

Derive the next identifier for a numbered type from the built index rather
than from a filesystem walk, so the query costs a lookup.

**Verification timing:** AC-SPEC-011.4 (the `next-id` subcommand) is proved
by the CLI item, which lands in stage 2. This item proves AC-SPEC-007.1 at
unit level against the built index.

## Retro

Before closing this item, record retro findings on this issue —
one `bd comment` per finding, prefixed `retro:` — following the
findings capture protocol in `rfcs/findings-capture.md`. Friction
only: what happened plus the item or spec text that caused it (or
the gap where guidance was missing). No analysis, no RFCs — the
plan's final DoD item runs the aggregated retro.
design:
WHEN asked for the next identifier for a type the active profile registers as
numbered, return one greater than the highest number in use for that type

not affect the answer — that is the point of reading the index rather than
walking the tree.

Anchors: a new package under `cli/core` (e.g. `cli/core/numbering`); reads
the `SpecIndex` produced by the Corpus item and the numbered-type table
supplied through the `Profile` interface.

- [ ] The next identifier for a numbered type is one greater than the highest
      in use for that type anywhere in the corpus, independent of directory

title: Validate frontmatter against the profile's union schema
description:
**Blueprint:** `specs/features/spec-index/spec-index-blueprint.md` — delta **SR**, section "Schema Registry in module-document-core (added)".
**FRD:** `specs/features/spec-index/spec-index-frd.md`.
**Delivery:** staged (stage 1 of 3); this feature's closure set is `bd list --label feature-spec-validation-cli`.

Validate a document's frontmatter against the single union schema the active
profile supplies, dispatching by the document's `type` to the matching branch
of that union, and report every violation in one pass. Document Core stays
framework-agnostic: it compiles one schema from whichever profile is active
and never knows a `type` by name.

There is **no per-type schema registration** — a profile has one schema, not
a registry of them. This narrows the design in
`specs/architecture/module-spec-profile.md` and is one of the blueprint's Key
Decisions.

**Verification timing:** AC-SPEC-003.1 and AC-SPEC-003.5 name the PROF item
as a participating delta, and the blueprint notes PROF "is required for SR
and CO to check a conforming corpus green". PROF is not in this item's
dependency closure (the blueprint orders SR before PROF). Build and unit-test
against a fixture profile supplying a fixture union schema; green-corpus
verification arrives with the profile self-application item, and the final
DoD item is the backstop.

## Retro

Before closing this item, record retro findings on this issue —
one `bd comment` per finding, prefixed `retro:` — following the
findings capture protocol in `rfcs/findings-capture.md`. Friction
only: what happened plus the item or spec text that caused it (or
the gap where guidance was missing). No analysis, no RFCs — the
plan's final DoD item runs the aggregated retro.
design:
Accept one JSON Schema from the active profile — a discriminated union over
the profile's document types — and compile it once.

WHEN validating a document, validate its frontmatter against the branch of
that union selected by the document's `type`, reporting **every** violation
(not the first) as a `Finding` carrying the JSON Pointer at which it
occurred. Where the schema constrains textual format, validate the raw
property text the #Frontmatter item retained, not the YAML-coerced value.

WHEN a document's `slug` does not match the pattern the active profile
supplies for its `type`, report a `Finding` naming **both** the actual slug
and the expected pattern. The slug pattern comes from the profile's type
table, not the union schema, because Strata cannot narrow the inherited
`slug` per type.

Anchors: a new package under `cli/core` — the implementing agent chooses the
name, distinct from the generated `cli/core/schema/*.json` outputs.
[[adr-015]] names `santhosh-tekuri/jsonschema`. The union schema is the
bundle `scripts/generate-schemas.sh` emits
(`cli/core/schema/spec-model.schema.json`).
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] One union schema from the active profile is compiled once and validated
      against per document `type`, with every violation reported as a
      `Finding` carrying its JSON Pointer (**proves AC-SPEC-003.1**, unit).
- [ ] Where the schema constrains textual format, the retained raw property
      text is validated rather than the coerced value (**proves
      AC-SPEC-003.2**, unit).
- [ ] A slug not matching its type's pattern yields a `Finding` naming the
      actual slug and the expected pattern (**proves AC-SPEC-003.5**, unit).
- [ ] Multiple violations in one document are all reported in a single pass.
- [ ] No document type is named anywhere in this package.
- [ ] Unit tests cite AC-SPEC-003.1, 003.2 and 003.5. Tests cite the ACs they verify with an `// AC: AC-SPEC-XXX.Y` comment on the line immediately preceding the test declaration, per `specs/standards/testing-standards.md`.
- [ ] The Schema Registry component is recorded in
      `specs/architecture/module-document-core.md` as performing
      **single-union** validation, delivered in this same change.

metadata.tier_reason: Three clearly-specified ACs, localized to one package, with the union schema and the jsonschema library both supplied. Mostly execution; the union-branch dispatch is the only design call and the blueprint states it.

title: Build the spec-driven-dev profile
description:
**Blueprint:** `specs/features/spec-index/spec-index-blueprint.md` — delta **PROF**, section "spec-driven-dev profile in module-spec-profile (added)".
**FRD:** `specs/features/spec-index/spec-index-frd.md`.
**Delivery:** staged (stage 1 of 3); this feature's closure set is `bd list --label feature-spec-validation-cli`.

Supply this framework's vocabulary as one pluggable profile, not a per-type
registry. The profile carries a single union schema covering every document
type (the Strata bundle), a thin type table giving — per type — its slug
pattern and whether it is numbered, and the convention defaults; and it
exposes itself through Document Core's `Profile` extension point.

A different taxonomy is a different profile, selected by name from the
profile registry (the CFG item) — the customization path v1 supports, with no
per-type schema plumbing. Element records, required sections, reference
properties and lifecycle rules are added by later features; this delta
supplies only what this sprint's checks consume.

**Verification timing:** AC-SPEC-008.6 is verified at *integration* level and
names CFG as a participating delta — a profile "registers under the name
`spec-driven-dev` so an adopting repository activates it without authoring
one", and activation runs through the CFG item's profile registry, which
lands after this one. Unit-level registration can be proven here; the
integration citation belongs with CFG. The final DoD item is the backstop.

## Retro

Before closing this item, record retro findings on this issue —
one `bd comment` per finding, prefixed `retro:` — following the
findings capture protocol in `rfcs/findings-capture.md`. Friction
only: what happened plus the item or spec text that caused it (or
the gap where guidance was missing). No analysis, no RFCs — the
plan's final DoD item runs the aggregated retro.
design:
New package `cli/profile`.

- Expose one `New` constructor returning a value satisfying Document Core's
  `Profile` interface.
- Embed the bundled union schema via Go's `//go:embed` and supply it to the
  Schema Registry as the one schema all its document types validate against,
  so the binary carries the schema and reads no schema file at runtime. The
  embedded file is the generated
  `cli/core/schema/spec-model.schema.json`.
- Supply, per document type in the `DocumentType` vocabulary, its slug
  pattern and whether it is numbered — a thin table, not a per-type schema.
- Supply the `line_width` default the CLI resolves when `specs.toml` omits
  `[conventions].line_width` (see
  `specs/contracts/contract-specs-configuration.md`).
- Register under the name `spec-driven-dev`.

The per-type table maps onto the existing `slug_pattern` and `numbered`
fields of `DocumentTypeRegistration` in `cli/core/specmodel`. That struct's
`schema` field is **unused in v1**, since one union schema serves every type
— leave it unpopulated rather than inventing a use.

This collapses `specs/architecture/module-spec-profile.md`'s separate
Document Types "type registry" component; that blueprint is reconciled by the
blueprint-reconciliation item, not here.

`specs/architecture/module-spec-profile.md` Change Guidance: this module must
not implement parsing, indexing or reference resolution, and must not require
a change to the `Profile` interface for a framework-specific reason.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] `cli/profile.New` returns a value satisfying Document Core's `Profile`
      interface, registered under the name `spec-driven-dev` (**proves
      AC-SPEC-008.6**, integration — see the verification-timing note; the
      end-to-end activation citation may land with the CFG item).
- [ ] The union schema is embedded via `//go:embed`; the binary reads no
      schema file at runtime (participates in AC-SPEC-009.4).
- [ ] A per-type table supplies slug pattern and numbered-ness for every
      `DocumentType` (participates in AC-SPEC-003.5 and AC-SPEC-007.1).
- [ ] The `line_width` convention default is supplied (participates in
      AC-SPEC-008.2).
- [ ] A conformance test asserts this module satisfies the `Profile`
      interface (the module's Change Guidance gate).
- [ ] No parsing, indexing or reference-resolution logic lives in
      `cli/profile`.
- [ ] `go test ./profile/...` passes.
- [ ] The single-schema profile is confirmed as built in
      `specs/architecture/module-spec-profile.md`, delivered in this same

title: Add the Finding model, severity vocabulary and report rendering
description:
**Blueprint:** `specs/features/spec-index/spec-index-blueprint.md` — delta **FIND**, section "#Findings in module-document-core (added)".
**FRD:** `specs/features/spec-index/spec-index-frd.md`.
**Delivery:** staged (stage 1 of 3); this feature's closure set is `bd list --label feature-spec-validation-cli`.

One finding model and one severity vocabulary must carry every check's
output, so the command surface renders one shape and later features add
checks without changing it. The finding JSON is a published interface surface
— an agent parses it — so its shape is defined in Strata alongside the index
model and generated, not hand-rolled in Go. Establishing this early is what
makes the AC-SPEC-006.1 self-contained-diagnostic guarantee uniform.

## Retro

Before closing this item, record retro findings on this issue —
one `bd comment` per finding, prefixed `retro:` — following the
findings capture protocol in `rfcs/findings-capture.md`. Friction
only: what happened plus the item or spec text that caused it (or
the gap where guidance was missing). No analysis, no RFCs — the
plan's final DoD item runs the aggregated retro.
design:
**Model (Strata source under `schemas/`, e.g. `finding.strata`)**, generated
into the same JSON-Schema/Go/Markdown outputs as every other model per
[[adr-016]]:

- a base `Finding` struct carrying a stable rule identifier, a severity (enum
  `error` | `warning` | `unverified`), a repository-relative path, a `Span`,
  and a message;
- a **discriminated union of finding variants** keyed by the rule (or a
  `kind` discriminator), each adding the structured fields that make the
  finding self-contained — a slug-pattern variant carrying the actual slug
  and the expected pattern, a missing-property variant carrying the property
  name, a duplicate-slug variant carrying the other document's path. The
  message is derivable from the variant, so a consumer branches on structure
  rather than parsing prose;
- a report envelope carrying, per check requested, whether it ran, so the
  JSON distinguishes "check passed" from "check not requested".

**Behavior** (a new package under `cli/core`, e.g. `cli/core/finding`): a
check that was requested but could not run is represented as `unverified`,
never as passed. The report serialises both as human-readable text and as the
generated finding JSON, so the command surface selects a rendering rather
than formatting findings itself.

**Scope cuts the blueprint pins:** build the `unverified` mechanism but
register no check that emits it (the mermaid example in AC-SPEC-006.3 is a
structure-feature concern). Define only the finding variants this sprint's
checks raise; later features add variants without changing the envelope.

**Shared-artifact edge:** this item depends on IDX because both add a Strata
source under `schemas/` and regenerate the same `cli/core/specmodel` output.
The edge is there to avoid hand-resolving generated-file conflicts, not
because the finding model needs the index model.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] A Strata source under `schemas/` declares the base `Finding`, the
      severity enum, the variant union and the report envelope.
- [ ] A finding is self-contained: rule id, severity, path, `Span`, message,
      plus the variant's structured fields (**proves AC-SPEC-006.1**, unit).
- [ ] A requested-but-unrunnable check is represented as `unverified`, never
      as passed (**proves AC-SPEC-006.3, AC-SPEC-006.4**, unit).
- [ ] The report distinguishes a passed check from an un-requested one
      (**proves AC-SPEC-006.9**, unit).
- [ ] The report serialises as both human-readable text and the generated
      finding JSON.
- [ ] Generated artifacts are regenerated and `scripts/generate-schemas.sh
      --check` passes.
- [ ] Unit tests cite AC-SPEC-006.1, 006.3, 006.4 and 006.9. Tests cite the ACs they verify with an `// AC: AC-SPEC-XXX.Y` comment on the line immediately preceding the test declaration, per `specs/standards/testing-standards.md`.
- [ ] The Findings component and the `Finding` model are recorded in
      `specs/architecture/module-document-core.md`, delivered in this same
      change.

metadata.tier_reason: Discriminated-union design for a published interface surface an agent parses, plus a severity model and dual text/JSON rendering. Getting the variant shape wrong is costly once later features extend the union.

title: Parse frontmatter to a generic model retaining raw property text
description:
**Blueprint:** `specs/features/spec-index/spec-index-blueprint.md` — delta **FM**, section "#Frontmatter in module-document-core (added)".

that preserves each property's raw text, feeding both schema validation and
typed decoding. Raw-text retention is what lets AC-SPEC-003.2 validate what
the author *wrote* rather than what YAML inferred (e.g. an unquoted date that
YAML would hand back as a timestamp).

**Verification timing:** this delta proves no AC on its own. It participates
in AC-SPEC-002.4 (proved by the CO item) and AC-SPEC-003.2 (proved by the SR
item), both of which land after this one. Code work here proceeds as soon as
the item is ready; the ACs it participates in are cited from those downstream
items' tests, and the plan's final DoD item is the backstop.

Before closing this item, record retro findings on this issue —
one `bd comment` per finding, prefixed `retro:` — following the
findings capture protocol in `rfcs/findings-capture.md`. Friction
only: what happened plus the item or spec text that caused it (or
the gap where guidance was missing). No analysis, no RFCs — the

scan for `---` independently; the module's Change Guidance requires new
parsing capability to build on that scanner. Parse the region to a generic
document model, retaining the raw source text of each property alongside its
parsed value.

rather than raising, so the caller (the Corpus item) records the failure
against that member and continues indexing the rest.

- [ ] A document whose frontmatter fails to parse yields a located parse

- [ ] Unit tests cover: valid frontmatter, absent frontmatter, malformed

description:
**Blueprint:** `specs/features/spec-index/spec-index-blueprint.md` — delta **CO**, section "Sequencing Constraints — the foundational `Profile` sliver".

The `Profile` extension point is the seam through which a profile supplies
its union schema, slug patterns and numbered types to the framework-agnostic

> The `Profile` extension-point interface (in package `cli/core/corpus`) —
> the surface through which a profile supplies its union schema, slug
> patterns and numbered types — is a foundational sliver: it SHALL be
> defined before the PROF delta implements it and before the CO and CFG
> deltas consume it, i.e. ahead of the CO delta's own discovery logic even
> though both live in that package. Grooming SHOULD lift it into its own
> early work item.

This is that item. It exists because three later items (PROF implements it,
CO and CFG consume it) would otherwise each be blocked on the whole of CO.

**Provenance note:** this work order derives from a Sequencing Constraint
rather than from its own delta block, so it is stamped `delta:CO` — the
delta that owns package `cli/core/corpus`. Re-grooming will see two items
carrying `delta:CO`: this seam and the CO discovery logic.

Before closing this item, record retro findings on this issue —
one `bd comment` per finding, prefixed `retro:` — following the
findings capture protocol in `rfcs/findings-capture.md`. Friction
only: what happened plus the item or spec text that caused it (or
the gap where guidance was missing). No analysis, no RFCs — the

Define the `Profile` interface in `cli/core/corpus`, exposing exactly what
this sprint's consumers need and nothing more:

  discriminated union over those types);

title: triage-rfc: check a proposal's extent and sufficiency before adopting (RFC P1)
description:
## Problem

The `triage-rfc` skill verifies that an RFC's quoted evidence EXISTS in
the tree, but never that the evidence is COMPLETE, nor that the proposed
change covers the evidence it cites. Every existing check points at
existence only:

- `.claude/skills/triage-rfc/SKILL.md:270` anti-pattern row: "Adopting
  on plausibility without verifying the quoted evidence" — checks the
  quote is really there.
- `SKILL.md:111` adopt-now criteria: "concrete change, verbatim
  evidence, small blast radius" — none is an extent check.
- `SKILL.md:221` verify bullet: "Re-read each file you changed" —
  scoped to files that DID change, so a file that should have changed
  and did not is outside it by construction.

## Evidence (inlined — do not rely on the RFC being at hand)

Observed in the triage run of 2026-08-01, model claude-opus-5.

EXTENT. RFC 0007 P1 cited four occurrences of retired `@` notation in
three templates. The real count was six in five files:

    $ grep -rn '@<' plugin/skills/
    .../module-blueprint-template.md:317
    .../container-blueprint-template.md:323
    .../component-blueprint-template.md:193
    .../contract-template.md:108
    .../contract-template.md:202
    .../system-blueprint-template.md:219

`component-blueprint-template.md:193` and
`system-blueprint-template.md:219` were never cited — the authoring run
that produced the RFC never opened those two files. The sweep happened
only because that RFC's author wrote "Triage should also sweep the
remaining templates" into the proposal body. Nothing in the skill asks
for it. Adopting P1 as cited would have left two templates emitting
prohibited syntax while the Resolution recorded the class as fixed —
the exact outcome `SKILL.md:223` warns against ("A half-applied
adoption is worse than a deferral, because the Resolution will claim it
landed").

SUFFICIENCY. RFC 0007 P2's proposed text told the reader to assign "a
jsdom `window` and `document` onto `globalThis`". That same RFC's
finding 2 states six globals were needed: `window`, `document`,
`navigator`, `Element`, `HTMLElement`, `SVGElement`. The proposed fix
was inconsistent with the evidence in its own document; adopting it
verbatim would have shipped guidance that still fails.

Source: rfcs/inbox/triage-rfc/rfc-self-triage-rfc-evidence-completeness.md,
proposal P1 (severity blocker, origin self, runs_observed 1).
design:
Insert after step 3's classification list (after the
`already-implemented` bullet, before the line `4. **Present the
recommendation and STOP for approval.**`), at 3-space indent to match
the surrounding step body:

   Before classifying a proposal **adopt-now**, run two checks its
   author could not have run. Both are triage's, and each has a
   recorded outcome:

   - **Extent.** WHEN the evidence cites occurrences of a repeatable
     pattern — a syntax, a phrase, a defect class — enumerate that
     pattern across the whole surface before adopting. A cited list is
     a sample from one run's path, not a census: the reporting run only
     opened the files its task required. Put the enumerating command
     and its result in the Resolution.
   - **Sufficiency.** Read the proposed Change against the finding it
     cites. WHEN the change resolves less than its own evidence
     describes, widen it and adopt with refinement.

   Failing either check does not sink a proposal — it resizes it. A
   proposal whose extent was understated is adopted with refinement
   over the full set, not rejected.

Then append this row to the Anti-Patterns table at the end of the file
(table cells are exempt from the 80-column rule):

| Treating a proposal's cited occurrences as the complete set | The RFC lists what its run touched; a defect class usually reaches files that run never opened, and the Resolution then records as fixed a class that is still live |

Do NOT bump the skill version in this bead — agent-plugins bead for P5
owns the single 1.3 -> 1.4 bump and is last in this chain.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Step 3 carries an Extent check and a Sufficiency check, inserted after the already-implemented bullet
- [ ] The Anti-Patterns table has a row about treating cited occurrences as the complete set
- [ ] Every line added outside a table row is at most 80 characters
- [ ] The skill frontmatter version is NOT changed by this bead
notes: Tier: standard. tier_reason: the wording is supplied verbatim, but it lands in two separate regions of the file (step 3 body and the trailing table) and the table row must be recognised as width-exempt while the prose is not. No C4 component is affected; this file is a skill, not a documented container or module.

title: ADR: index cache invalidation

title: triage-rfc: make already-implemented vs reject-already-addressed distinguishable (triage T1)
description:
## Problem

`.claude/skills/triage-rfc/SKILL.md:120-126` defines the
`already-implemented` classification and distinguishes it from
`reject — already addressed` with a single clause: "which is for a
proposal whose premise no longer holds". A human reader of the skill
reported that this does not convey the distinction, because in BOTH
cases the change is already present in the tree, so "the premise no
longer holds" appears to describe both.

Current text at SKILL.md:120-126:

    - **already-implemented** — the proposal is sound and its change is
      already present in the tree, landed by earlier work rather than by
      this triage. Distinct from `reject — already addressed`, which is
      for a proposal whose premise no longer holds: this one was right
      and nothing about it is being turned down. Record it in the
      Resolution as "adopted — already implemented", name where the
      change lives, and bump nothing.

## Evidence (inlined — do not rely on the RFC being at hand)

Reported directly by the repository owner on 2026-08-01, quoting
SKILL.md:122 and stating: "This does not make it clear (to me) what the
distinction between `reject - already addressed` and `adopted - already
implemented`."

This is a triage-originated work order (id T1), not a proposal from a
received RFC. It has no reporting RFC; the reporter is the human gate.

The distinction that the text should convey, and currently does not:
both outcomes mean the change is already in the tree, but they differ
in whether triage is ruling on the proposal's MERITS at all.
`adopted — already implemented` affirms the proposal was correct;
`reject — already addressed` takes no position, because the thing the
proposal targeted no longer exists. The consequence is load-bearing at
step 2, which reads prior Resolutions during dedupe: "adopted" means
settled, do not relitigate; "rejected — already addressed" means only
that the evidence was stale, so the same idea with fresh evidence gets
a fresh hearing.
design:
Replace the `already-implemented` bullet at SKILL.md:120-126 with:

   - **already-implemented** — the proposal is sound and its change is
     already present in the tree, landed by earlier work rather than by
     this triage. Record it in the Resolution as "adopted — already
     implemented", name where the change lives, and bump nothing.

     The test against `reject — already addressed` is whether triage is
     ruling on the proposal's merits at all. Use **already-implemented**
     WHEN you would have adopted it had the tree been untouched: the
     proposal was right, and this triage says so. Use **reject —
     already addressed** WHEN there is nothing to rule on — the text it
     quotes is gone or rewritten, so its premise fails and triage takes
     no position on whether the idea was ever good.

     The difference is load-bearing at step 2, which reads prior
     Resolutions. "Adopted" tells a future triage the idea is settled
     and should not be relitigated; "rejected — already addressed"
     tells it only that the evidence was stale, so the same idea backed
     by fresh evidence gets a fresh hearing.

Keep the bullet in place in step 3's list; do not reorder the
classifications. Do NOT bump the skill version in this bead.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] The already-implemented bullet states the merits test (would you have adopted it had the tree been untouched)

- [ ] It names the step-2 dedupe consequence for both outcomes
- [ ] Every line added is at most 80 characters
- [ ] The skill frontmatter version is NOT changed by this bead

title: No merge strategy for .beads/issues.jsonl — beads created on two branches will conflict
description:
`.beads/issues.jsonl` is the only carrier of issues between sessions and branches in this project (see the 'How beads persist in THIS project' section of CLAUDE.md). There is no `.gitattributes` in the repo, so git merges it as ordinary text.

Two branches that each create beads produce overlapping line-level edits in one file. Git will report a conflict, and the natural resolutions are both wrong: taking one side drops the other branch's issues, and a careless union can duplicate ids or interleave a partial record.

The failure is silent in the worst case — a conflict resolved by 'keep mine' loses issues that were correctly exported and committed, which is exactly the loss the export discipline exists to prevent.

## Options to evaluate
- A `.gitattributes` union merge driver for the file. Cheap, but union can produce two lines with the same id when both branches touched one issue, so it needs an id-dedupe pass afterwards.
- A custom merge driver that parses JSONL, keys by id, and prefers the higher `updated_at`. Correct, but needs a script every clone can run.
- Regenerate from the database after merge rather than merging the file: resolve by taking either side, then `bd import` both versions and `bd export` fresh. Uses beads' own conflict handling.
- Whether beads upstream ships a documented driver for this — check before building one.
acceptance_criteria: A documented, tested procedure for merging two branches that both added beads, with no issue lost and no duplicate id in the resulting .beads/issues.jsonl

title: Index: model references as a separate edge collection, not only object properties
description:
Architectural input for the index-schema ADR (not yet written). Raised in PR #4 review of the FRD, 2026-07-31, explicitly flagged as 'not a comment for the FRD, but an architectural one for later'.

## The proposal

The index should collect the domain's model objects — specs
('documents'), systems, containers, components, and eventually features
— AND separately build a collection of REFERENCES that behave like
edges in a graph rather than like members of the objects they connect.
Each reference carries the file and span where it occurs.

Rationale given: this makes references queryable independently of the
objects. 'What points at adr-007?' becomes an edge query rather than a
scan over every object's properties.

This does not mean relationships never live inside objects. Some
belong there — a 'component' object might carry an injected
'container' property naming its parent. The proposal is specifically
about references that occur INSIDE document bodies: those are better
modelled as edges.

## Why it is not in the FRD

The FRD (docs/frds/FRD-spec-validation-cli.md) states WHAT the index
must contain, and AC-SPEC-002.1 and AC-SPEC-002.5 already require
outbound and inbound references. HOW the index is shaped — one
collection of objects with embedded arrays, versus objects plus a
separate edge collection — is a schema design decision, and the FRD
deliberately defers index schema and versioning to an ADR.

## Why it matters more than it looks

AC-SPEC-002.2 makes the index schema a published API with a version
identifier, and AC-SPEC-002.3 requires a workspace identifier so
indexes from separate repositories merge into one graph. An edge
collection is materially easier to merge across repositories than
embedded arrays, because edges from repo A pointing at objects in repo
B are just rows — whereas embedded arrays require rewriting the source
object. Getting this wrong is expensive to change after publication.

## Related decisions already made

- Reference relationships are DERIVED from body wikilinks, not
  hand-maintained frontmatter (settled in review; see
  docs/plans/spec-validation-cli-brief.md section 3).
- A 'span' carries a byte offset and length plus line/column, so an
  edge can record exactly where in the source the reference occurs
  (FRD Terminology, revised 2026-07-31).
design:
Input to the index-schema ADR; not standalone work. The ADR must decide:

1. Objects-with-embedded-arrays vs objects-plus-edge-collection vs both.
2. IF both, which relationships live where, and how duplication between
   the two representations is prevented from drifting.
3. Whether edges are typed (references / parent / supersedes / composes)
   or uniform with a 'kind' discriminator.
4. How edges behave across a workspace boundary when the target object
   is not in this repository's index.

Do not implement ahead of that ADR — the index schema is a published
API under AC-SPEC-002.2 and changing it later is the expensive case.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] The index-schema ADR records a decision on object-vs-edge representation, with this proposal weighed in Alternatives Considered.
- [ ] The decision addresses cross-repository merge, since that is the case that most distinguishes the options.
- [ ] IF edges are adopted, the FRD's AC-SPEC-002.1 and AC-SPEC-002.5 are re-examined for consistency with the chosen shape.

title: triage-rfc: should the sequencing escape hatch key on the graph's consumer? (RFC P4)
description:
DEFERRED at triage on 2026-08-01. Not dispatchable as written — the
evidence is self-referential and one more independent observation is
wanted before the rule is changed. Status is 'deferred' so it stays out
of 'bd ready'.

## Problem

`.claude/skills/triage-rfc/SKILL.md:173-175` gives the escape hatch
from the sequencing rule:

    WHERE the approved set is small and touches disjoint files,
    implement inline and say so; grooming a two-file change is
    overhead.

The hatch turns on the SHAPE of the approved set — size and file
disjointness. The variable that has actually decided the question in
practice is different: whether anything will CONSUME the dependency
graph that grooming produces. A single agent implementing inline, with
no dispatch and no parallelism, produces a graph with no reader.

## Evidence (inlined — do not rely on the RFC being at hand)

Two observations, both from model claude-opus-5, both in the session of
2026-08-01, and both made by the agent that authored the rule.

1. The triage that ADOPTED this rule (RFC 0008 P1) then declined to
   follow it. Its approved set was 10 proposals with 6 colliding on one
   file — neither small nor disjoint, so the hatch did not apply and
   the rule required filing 10 beads and running `groom-beads`. The
   agent implemented inline and recorded the deviation in
   `rfcs/rfc-0008-triage-rfc-implementation-sequencing.md` under
   Resolution. Its stated reason was the missing consumer, not the set
   shape. Correctness the rule protects — serialized edits to a shared
   file, version bump last — was obtained by hand and verified.

2. The next triage run hit the same fork: 5 approved changes plus one
   human-reported change, all landing on the same file. The human was
   asked to choose and directed that the rule be followed, which is how
   the beads for that run (including this one) came to exist.

## Why this was deferred rather than adopted

Both observations are the same agent in the same session, so this is
repetition rather than independent corroboration. The RFC proposing it
says so itself: "Triage may reasonably defer it for corroboration from
a run that did not author it."

The cost of deferring is real and should be weighed on any future
recurrence: the rule stays miscalibrated, and the next single-agent
triage either files beads nobody reads or deviates again.

## What would make this ready

Any ONE of:
- A triage run under a different model, or in a different session,
  hitting the same fork and recording what it did.
- A decision that filing the graph is worth it regardless of consumer
  (e.g. because the beads are themselves the audit record) — which
  would close this by rejecting it, not by adopting it.

## The proposed change, if it is ever adopted

Replace SKILL.md:173-175 with:

     WHERE the approved set is small and touches disjoint files, OR
     WHERE the implementation will run in a single agent with no
     dispatch and no parallelism, implement inline and say so —
     sequencing the colliding edits by hand and bumping each file after
     its last change, which is what the graph would have enforced. File
     the graph when something will consume it: parallel agents, a
     `bead-bonanza` run, or work resuming in a later session. A graph
     with no reader is filing, not sequencing.

title: bd auto-export does not propagate deletions to issues.jsonl
description:
Measured 2026-07-31 in this repo, bd 1.1.2, with `export.auto: true` and `interval: 60s` in .beads/config.yaml.

Creating an issue refreshed .beads/issues.jsonl immediately (10 lines to 19). `bd delete` on that same issue did NOT: the deleted record was still in the file after 90 seconds, well past the interval. Only an explicit `bd export > .beads/issues.jsonl` produced a correct file (18 lines, probe absent).

Consequence in this project: because the SessionStart hook rebuilds the database by importing that file, a deleted issue silently comes back in the next session.

Worked around by documenting the explicit export in the session-close steps in CLAUDE.md and AGENTS.md. Worth reporting upstream, and worth re-testing on a bd upgrade — if auto export becomes authoritative the manual step can go.
acceptance_criteria: Either upstream fixes it and the manual export step is removed from CLAUDE.md, or the limitation is confirmed as intended and the workaround stays with a link to the upstream decision
notes: Follow-up test 2026-07-31: the beads PRE-COMMIT hook uses the same append/update path, so it does not rescue a deletion either. Sequence: create probe -> commit (file gains it, 21 lines) -> bd delete probe -> commit again (file STILL has it, 21 lines). An earlier commit that printed 'Exported 20 issues' and produced a correct file was correct only because an explicit bd export had been run moments before. Conclusion: an explicit 'bd export > .beads/issues.jsonl' is the only form that reflects deletions.

title: frontmatter: can 'sources' record an input that is not a spec document? (RFC 0006 P4)
description:
DEFERRED at triage on 2026-07-31. Not dispatchable as written — the scope decision below is unmade. Status is 'deferred' so it stays out of 'bd ready'.

## Problem

A 'sources' frontmatter property is defined as holding SLUGS ONLY:
'plugin/skills/spec/references/frontmatter-standards.md:119' declares
'sources: []   # Source document slugs'. The FRD template repeats it at
'plugin/skills/spec/references/frd-template.md:8' — 'slugs of documents
this FRD is based on'.

But documents outside the specification set have no slug BY DESIGN.
'plugin/skills/spec/references/cross-document-references.md:124-125'
states: 'The [[document-slug]] notation SHALL be reserved for documents
in the specification set; it SHALL NOT be used for documents outside
it.' Research briefs, vendor docs and prior-art reviews are correctly
out-of-set and correctly slugless.

So an FRD derived from an out-of-set input cannot record that fact.

## Evidence (inlined — do not rely on the RFC being at hand)

'docs/frds/FRD-spec-validation-cli.md' was derived almost entirely from
'docs/plans/spec-validation-cli-brief.md', a ~700-line research brief
carrying prototype measurements and nine resolved scope questions. The
brief is correctly not a spec document and correctly has no slug. The
FRD therefore ships with 'sources: []' — which is FALSE. Its only record
of provenance is one backticked path in the References prose section.

The index specified by that same FRD (REQ-SPEC-002) would report the
document as having no sources at all.

## Why this was deferred rather than adopted

The RFC proposed changing 'frd-template.md:8' alone. Triage rejected
that scope: 'frontmatter-standards.md' OWNS the property, so changing
one template alone would make a template contradict its standard — which
is precisely the defect class P1 of the same RFC was adopted to remove
(the ADR template contradicting the prefix registry, which produced 11
non-conforming slugs and 26 dangling references).

Three templates carry a 'sources' property:
  plugin/skills/spec/references/frd-template.md
  plugin/skills/spec/references/feature-blueprint-template.md
  plugin/skills/spec/references/work-order-template.md

## What must be decided before this is groomable

1. Should 'sources' accept a mixed list (slugs for in-set documents,
   repo-relative paths for out-of-set ones), or should a SECOND property
   carry out-of-set inputs? A mixed list keeps one property but makes
   every consumer discriminate two value shapes; a second property keeps
   each shape clean but adds vocabulary to a deliberately small set.
2. Whichever is chosen, 'frontmatter-standards.md' changes FIRST as the
   owner, then the three templates follow in the same change.
3. Does the same treatment apply to 'related', which has the identical
   slugs-only constraint?

Source: rfcs/rfc-0006-spec-reference-bundles-and-adr-slug.md, proposal
P4. Retro that produced it: rfcs/retro-note-frd-authoring-2026-07-31.md
design:
NOT AN IMPLEMENTATION PLAN — the three questions above are unmade decisions. A grooming pass can only start once a human picks (1) and confirms (3).

Whichever shape wins, the change ORDER is fixed: frontmatter-standards.md (the owner) first, then frd-template.md, feature-blueprint-template.md and work-order-template.md in the same commit, each with its instruction-block Version bumped, plus the plugin version. Landing a template ahead of the standard reproduces the exact contradiction P1 was adopted to remove.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] A human has chosen mixed-list vs second-property, and answered whether 'related' gets the same treatment.
- [ ] frontmatter-standards.md defines the chosen form, and its version is bumped.
- [ ] All three templates carrying 'sources' match that definition, each with its instruction-block Version bumped.
- [ ] No template states a rule about 'sources' that frontmatter-standards.md does not.
- [ ] scripts/check-skills.sh exits 0.

title: templates: placeholder section lists convey nothing (RFC P4)
description:
GROOMING OUTCOME: blocked-ungroomable. NOT dispatchable. Do not hand
this bead to an implementing agent — the change it describes is defective
as written and its scope is undecided. See "Why this is blocked" below
and the reshape requirements in Design. Status is `deferred` so it stays
out of `bd ready`.

Source: `rfcs/inbox/rfc-self-spec-document-self-check.md`, proposal P4
(severity polish, origin self, runs_observed 1, model claude-opus-5).
Filed by an RFC triage pass that stopped at step 4 on human instruction;
nothing was implemented. The triage recommendation was DEFER.

PROBLEM AS REPORTED
`plugin/skills/spec/references/standards-template.md:15-18` reads:

    Sections (complete each, then delete its instruction block)
      - <Major Category>
      - <Another Major Category>
      - References

For a template whose sections are author-defined, this enumerates
placeholders and conveys little. It contrasts with the fixed-section
templates — ADR (Context / Decision / Alternatives Considered /
Consequences / References) — where the same list is a genuine map.
The RFC proposes replacing the placeholder list with a structural note:
"Structure: one `##` per major requirement category, `###` per
subcategory, then a References section. Categories are author-defined;
name them for the domain, not for this template."

WHY THIS IS BLOCKED (three findings, all verified during grooming)

1. The proposed change breaks the repo's own gate.
   `scripts/check-skills.sh:132-136` fails any file under
   `plugin/skills/*/references/` longer than 100 lines that has no line
   matching `^#+ Contents` or `^Sections \(complete`:

       for p in glob.glob('plugin/skills/*/references/*.md'):
           if '/shared/' in p: continue
           t = open(p).read()
           if len(t.split('\n')) > 100 and not re.search(
                   r'^#+ Contents|^Sections \(complete', t, re.M):
               err(p, "over 100 lines with no table of contents")

   `standards-template.md` is 218 lines and clears that gate only via
   its line 15, "Sections (complete each, then delete its instruction
   block)" — the exact line P4 deletes. The RFC's replacement text
   matches neither alternation branch, so applying P4 verbatim makes
   `scripts/check-skills.sh` fail on the very file it edits.

2. The real scope is ten files, and the RFC specifies one.
   Ten templates under `plugin/skills/spec/references/` carry the same
   "Sections (complete each" construct — verified by grep: adr,
   component-blueprint, container-blueprint, contract, feature-blueprint,
   frd, module-blueprint, standards, system-blueprint, work-order. The
   RFC addresses only the author-defined-section case and does not say
   which of the ten keep their enumerated list. A dispatched agent would
   have to invent that taxonomy decision.

3. No run cost, so nothing forces the call now. The RFC's own
   justification is "worth doing while the section lists are being
   reviewed for other reasons" — it records no evidence that the
   placeholder list harmed a run.
design:
NOT AN IMPLEMENTATION PLAN. This bead is blocked-ungroomable; what
follows is what a human must decide before it can be re-groomed, and
what a reshaped change would have to satisfy.

UNBLOCK CRITERIA (any implementing work needs all three settled)

A. A human adopt/defer decision. The current recommendation is DEFER,
   pending a second, independent project reporting the same friction —
   at which point the `theme:template-ergonomics` label makes the
   recurrence countable.

B. A scope decision naming, of the ten templates carrying the
   "Sections (complete each" construct (adr, component-blueprint,
   container-blueprint, contract, feature-blueprint, frd,
   module-blueprint, standards, system-blueprint, work-order), which
   are in scope for the structural note and which keep their enumerated
   list. The RFC treats this as a one-file edit; it is not.

C. A gate strategy, picking exactly one of:
   - keep a line matching `^Sections \(complete` in every touched file
     over 100 lines; or
   - add a `## Contents` heading to every touched file over 100 lines;
     or
   - deliberately amend the regex at `scripts/check-skills.sh:135` to
     accept the new form, as its own reviewed change.

A reshaped bead would also have to bump each touched template's
instruction-block `Version`, plus
`plugin/.claude-plugin/plugin.json`.

WHY NOT blocked-needs-info: the block is not one missing fact. Even
given a human "adopt", the change still needs redesign (B and C), so
this is a redesign block, not an information block.
